title: Testing Whether SAE Feature Labels Generated by LLMs Are Faithful or Confabulatory

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if automated SAE labeling is unreliable, a large fraction of interpretability results may be artifacts. Directly affects credibility of SAE-based safety claims.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: load pre-trained SAE, collect top-activating examples, call GPT-4o-mini for labels, shuffle and re-label. Beginner-friendly with Python and API calls.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: 40 features, original vs. shuffled labels, human coherence rating. One clear metric (coherence gap between real and shuffled). Very feasible in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: The core concern (are LLM-generated SAE labels faithful?) has been addressed by multiple groups. EleutherAI's auto-interp library already uses shuffled-vs-real scoring. SAEBench evaluates concept detection fidelity. The Interpretability Illusions and Feature Sensitivity papers both test robustness of auto-interpretations. The specific shuffled-label confabulation test framing overlaps substantially with existing work, though a focused human coherence comparison adds modest novelty.

evidence.source: Open Source Automated Interpretability for SAE Features (EleutherAI, 2025)
evidence.finding: Introduces five scoring techniques for auto-interpretability of SAE features including shuffled-vs-real classification accuracy as a faithfulness metric.
Uses adversarial perturbations to assess robustness of SAE-derived interpretations, demonstrating that auto-interpreted labels can be fragile.
Provides a unified evaluation framework including Concept Detection metrics that assess how precisely individual latents correspond to meaningful concepts.
Tests whether features activate on LLM-generated text with same semantic properties as activating examples, finding many interpretable features have poor sensitivity.
